## Prompt 1 — Full‑stack Compatibility Audit (Next.js 14 App Router + Vercel Node runtime + our exact stack)

**Plain text**

You are a Staff+ full-stack engineer doing a "stop-ship" compatibility audit before we write any code.

**Project:** MOBreviews "Mob Reviews Growth Engine" (Next.js full-stack web app) for an invite-only dining membership + review network launching in Bangkok. Core business mechanics:
- Members pay $10–20/month and receive 25–50% off at partner restaurants when doing structured reviews.
- Reviews must follow a bell curve (cannot give everyone 5 stars).
- Each member maintains a personal ranked list ("My top 10 in Bangkok").
- Restaurants pay $200 to join.
- "Invisible until reveal": reviewer identity hidden until they reveal in-app to claim discount.
- Franchise/territory model: city operators buy business-in-a-box; influencers earn commission on franchise sales.

**Application scope (must be feasible on Vercel):**
- CRM: restaurants, influencers, franchise prospects, members
- AI research engine: generates prospect profiles from name/URL
- Personalized landing pages per prospect
- Outreach sequences + tracking + AI-generated copy
- Referral + franchise hierarchy + commission calculations
- AI chat (text + voice) connected to database data
- MCP server so an AI assistant can control the app via API from Telegram using OpenClaw
- Content publisher + GitHub Pages strategy site

**Locked tech stack (do not suggest alternatives; only identify issues + mitigations):**
- Next.js 14.x (App Router) + TypeScript 5.x
- Tailwind CSS 3.x + shadcn/ui
- Prisma 5.x + Turso (libSQL cloud; SQLite-compatible; Vercel-safe)
  - Uses @prisma/adapter-libsql + driverAdapters preview feature
- NextAuth.js v4 (NOT v5) — Google OAuth only

- OpenAI gpt-realtime via WebRTC for voice (browser connects directly to OpenAI; server provides session token endpoint)

**Your job:**
Find every version conflict, Vercel runtime limitation, App Router gotcha, deployment/runtime bug, and "commonly misimplemented" edge case for THIS exact stack. I do not want generic best practices. I want what breaks, why, how it manifests, and how to prevent it.

7) Content + community plan:
   - how to use "My top 10 in Bangkok" lists as a share object
   - what content formats work best in Thailand right now (with evidence)
   - a weekly publishing cadence tied to acquisition goals

**Constraints:**
- Avoid relying on paid ads as the main driver at launch.
- Assume we are a small team; prioritize the few highest-leverage actions.
- Cite sources for any market claims; distinguish "sourced" vs "inferred."

## Prompt 7 — Synthesis prompt: distill outputs of prompts 1–6 into a top‑25 pre‑build checklist

**Plain text**

You are a program manager + principal engineer. Your job is to turn research into an execution checklist.

**Inputs:**
I will paste the full outputs of six Deep Research runs:
1) Full-stack compatibility audit
2) OpenAI Realtime WebRTC implementation + gotchas
3) Turso + Prisma production plan
4) MCP + OpenClaw integration plan
5) Outreach + deliverability plan
6) Bangkok/SEA growth mechanics GTM plan

**Task:**
Synthesize the outputs into the top 25 "must not miss" items BEFORE writing a single line of code. These must be items where missing them causes:
- production outages,
- security incidents,
- deliverability/reputation damage,
- runaway AI costs,
- or GTM failure (restaurants won't join, members won't convert).

**Required output format:**

**A) Top 25 Pre-Build Checklist (table)**
Columns:
- Priority (P0/P1)
- Item (one sentence)
- Why it matters (consequence if missed)
- Owner role (backend, frontend, platform, growth, ops)
- Evidence (which prompt(s) it came from + short cited excerpt/summary)
- Validation test (how we confirm it's done)
- "Ship blocker?" (Yes/No)

**B) Risk register (top 10):**
- risk → probability → impact → early warning signals → mitigation plan

**C) "First 7 days build plan":**
- an ordered list of tasks that de-risks the stack fastest
- must include: a deployment smoke test, DB migration dry-run, webhook verification proof, and a minimal Realtime WebRTC demo behind auth

**Rules:**
- Do not add new ideas not present in the six outputs unless you label them clearly as "NEW INFERENCE."
- Prefer concrete, testable items over vague advice.
- If two items conflict (e.g., Vercel constraint vs MCP transport), surface the conflict explicitly and recommend the safer path.
